title: bls12-381-fixed-g1-invert-g2: Special Tower Number Field Sieve (STNFS) with derived sieve, low-merge Block-Wiedemann, and descent bounds

claims.statement: For uniform nonidentity P in G1 and uniform z in GT on BLS12-381, the Special Tower Number Field Sieve (STNFS) attack in proof.md computes g = e(P, Q0) in GT, recovers a in [0, r) satisfying g^a = z in F_{p^12}^* using the degree-6 tower h(Y) = Y^6 - Y^2 + 1 with f_y(X) = X^12 - 2*y*X^10 + 2*y^3*X^6 + y^5*X^2 + y^2 - 1 and g_y(X) = X^2 - u*y at parameters A = 686 and B = 2^65.316, and returns Q = [a]Q0 in G2 satisfying e(P, Q) = z. Under the STNFS smoothness, relation-yield, sparse-rank, and special-q descent heuristics disclosed and empirically checked in proof.md and experiment.py, the attack succeeds with probability at least 0.40 over uniform challenges and fresh algorithm coins (with an oversampling ratio lambda_orb / SP_orb >= 1.39 that preserves P(RF >= SP_orb) > 0.40 even under a 25% systematic downward modeling error in mean smoothness probability) using at most 2^118.860000 total target-group-operation equivalents (normalized by C = 20,000 scalar AArch64 instructions per reference dense F_{p^12} multiplication, corresponding to at most 2^133.142459 scalar AArch64 instructions). Peak memory is at most 2^73.000000 bytes (including 2,048 bytes per unfiltered relation, full 32-byte F_r matrix coefficients alongside 8-byte column indices, factor base tables, and Block-Wiedemann working vectors); preprocessing (charging all challenge-independent polynomial selection, factor base, sieving, and linear algebra stages in full without amortization) is at most 2^118.860000 target-group-operation equivalents and is included in total work; nonuniform advice is 0 bytes (2^0 bytes) and is included in memory.

experiments.purpose: Verify BLS12-381 STNFS polynomial identities and exact integer resultant norms in O_h = Z[y]/(y^6 - y^2 + 1) (including N_g(1+y, 0) = 1 and agreement with the 3 distinct complex conjugate-pair embeddings), validate empirical prime valuations and observe actual smooth relations on small-norm coprime pairs, compute 1/zeta_{K_h}(2) and exact TNFS Murphy alpha values alpha(f_y, h, B0) and alpha(g_y, h, B0), run Algorithm 6.1 at A = 686 and B = 2^65.316 with systematic error margin checks, and audit the complete instruction and memory ledgers.
